answer: At the kernel of this defence each identity must tend a portfolio of original work peers actually cite and build upon. A citation only counts from an independent identity with standing of its own, and the cited work must shape the citing work, so a ring of fakes citing each other is just an echo chamber with no weight. The portfolio grows like an orchard: every season it must yield new, checkable output, and duplicates are rejected on similarity. Faking one more identity means producing original work others find worth using, a cost that cannot be copied, shared, or parallelised away.
